the abdication crisis led to the first widespread public discussion of divorce .

not so . it had been a pressing social issue for some time . divorce was not only costly , beyond the reach of most except the very wealthy but anomalous . men could divorce women solely on the grounds of adultery but women had to prove additional grounds as well as adultery .
there was also the absurdity of partners who wished to divorce by mutual consent having to arrange a fake hotel adultery scenario .
it kept brighton hotels in business in the off season .

indeed , hence the proliferation of private " investigation " firms offering " confidential services " at a price including photographic evidence and an anonymous female co-respondent for couples whose marriage had broken down and wished to divorce .
and it 's still not ok ...

this applied to the then mrs simpson in 1936 too ( she alleged " unreasonable behaviour " in addition to her husband 's adultery ) . a royal commission had recommended liberalisation of the law as early as 1912 but an alliance of cofe bishops and liberal nonconformists prevented it .

ap herbert , the legal humorist , had written a best-selling novel " holy deadlock " in 1934 highlighting the injustices in the law and pursued a crusade after being elected as mp for oxford university to reform it

before baldwin , in one of his final acts as pm ( he retired in may 1937 ) , finally granted govt time to allow the bill to get through . it was the first reform of the divorce law since the matrimonial proceedings act of 1857 which set up the divorce court

its passage was facilitated by stanley baldwin in one of his last acts as pm .
